lead: Memphis faces severe storms, river and creek flooding, and winter freezes that strain old pipes. DryBeacon helps homes from Midtown to Cordova dry out fast.
risk: severe storms, creek flooding and freeze-burst pipes
why: In December 2022, a deep freeze burst pipes across Memphis, and water pressure dropped so far that the city issued a boil-water notice. The Mississippi River crested near record levels in 2011. Nonconnah Creek and the Wolf River flood neighborhoods in heavy rain.

Two-thirds of Memphis homes were built before 1980. Many older homes in Midtown and Cooper-Young have crawl spaces, older pipes and plaster. Tornadoes and straight-line winds bring down trees, and ice storms like the one in February 2023 cut power for days.
image_alt: Water leaking from a frozen pipe joint
image_caption: The December 2022 freeze burst pipes in homes across Memphis.
problems: Near Nonconnah Creek and the Wolf River
tips: Insulate crawl space pipes before winter.
Trim trees near the house before storm season.
areas: Calls come from Midtown, Cooper-Young, East Memphis, Downtown, Whitehaven, Hickory Hill, Cordova and Raleigh, plus Germantown, Collierville, Bartlett, Southaven and West Memphis.

faq.q: Why did so many pipes burst in Memphis in 2022?
faq.a: A long, deep freeze hit a city where many homes have pipes in crawl spaces and outside walls. Pipes froze and split, and leaks drained the water system. Insulating pipes and dripping faucets lower the risk.
